narration.text: Suppose a successful RUN leaves a new file with one hundred megabytes of uncompressed payload. In this ordinary unsquashed example, that payload becomes part of an immutable image layer.
A later RUN deletes the path. A whiteout hides it in the merged view, but the earlier layer still contains the payload. The whiteout is not an ordinary visible file in that merged view.
Now create and delete a NEW temporary file inside one RUN. The path is absent both before and after, so its payload is not added to that resulting diff. Other changes can still remain.
Do not apply that conclusion to a file already in the base layer. Deleting it still cannot rewrite the older layer or reclaim its bytes.
The one hundred megabytes is an assumption, not a measured image or download saving. Compression and cache use are different quantities. A running container also has a separate writable layer.
